LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.2: Rhythm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rhythm. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does one acquire the skill of composing rhythm in music?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe 3 4 time in music
2. compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time
3. perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time
4. appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RHYTHM
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rhythm helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RHYTHM
Study Rhythm like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe 3 4 time in music

What this means
In this part you learn to describe 3 4 time in music. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe 3 4 time in music.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe 3 4 time in music. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rhythm is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe 3 4 time in music)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words. (skill: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time)

Example 4: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate creating rhythms in 3 4 time)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rhythm to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe 3 4 time in music.
3. Practise this skill: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time.
4. Practise this skill: perform four-bar rhythmic patterns in 3 4 time.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rhythm from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rhythm: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Rhythm?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does one acquire the skill of composing rhythm in music?
2. What is the role of rhythm in day to day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rhythm means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe 3 4 time in music.
5. Be able to: compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3 4 time.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
